flagged.title: Energy Stores, Transfers and Power
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly instructs students that g is exactly 10 N/kg on Earth and to 'always always use 10' (and works through the calculation with 10 instead of 9.8 N/kg), which directly costs marks on AQA GCSE Physics exam papers.

mark_affecting.quote: the gravitational field strength g is exactly 10 newtons per kilogram on Earth... always always use 10

flagged.title: Domestic Electricity, Power and the National Grid
flagged.reason: The video states that alternating current at 50 Hz switches direction 50 times per second rather than completing 50 cycles per second (reversing direction 100 times per second), which is an explicit misconception that will cost GCSE marks.

mark_affecting.quote: So a frequency of 50 Hz, that means the current is physically changing direction 50 times every single second (also on-screen text at 01:42: 'switches direction 50 times/sec.')
